root_cause.text: The DWC3 gadget driver's dwc3_gadget_vbus_draw() directly called power_supply_set_property() from an atomic context, causing a sleep-in-atomic bug because the power-supply/PMIC path may sleep.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly states “dwc3_gadget_vbus_draw() can be called from atomic context” and that it “invokes power-supply-core APIs” where “some these PMIC APIs have operations that may sleep”; the patch removes the inline power_supply_set_property() call from gadget.c, stores mA in dwc->current_limit, and defers the property update via schedule_work() to the new dwc3_vbus_draw_work().

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE/commit explicitly states “dwc3_gadget_vbus_draw() can be called from atomic context” and that it “invokes power-supply-core APIs” where “some these PMIC APIs have operations that may sleep”; the patch removes the inline power_supply_set_property() call from gadget.c, stores mA in dwc->current_limit, and defers the property update via schedule_work() to the new dwc3_vbus_draw_work().

intent_record.intent_summary: Add deferred work to program the USB power supply input current limit from the DWC3 controller's current_limit setting.
intent_record.what: A new static workqueue callback function, dwc3_vbus_draw_work(struct work_struct *work), was added. It retrieves the enclosing struct dwc3 from the work item, initializes a power_supply_propval, sets val.intval to 1000 times dwc->current_limit, calls power_supply_set_property(dwc->usb_psy, POWER_SUPPLY_PROP_INPUT_CURRENT_LIMIT, &val), and logs a debug message if the call returns an error.
intent_record.how: This adds deferred runtime handling for updating the USB power supply's input current limit based on dwc->current_limit. When the work item is executed, it requests the power supply subsystem to set the VBUS draw/current limit and emits a debug log if that update fails.

intent_record.intent_summary: Initialize vbus_draw_work when acquiring the USB power supply so deferred VBUS draw handling can be safely scheduled.
intent_record.what: A new call to INIT_WORK(&dwc->vbus_draw_work, dwc3_vbus_draw_work) was added in dwc3_get_usb_power_supply() immediately before returning the usb power_supply pointer.
intent_record.how: This initializes the dwc->vbus_draw_work work item when the USB power supply is obtained, ensuring the deferred work structure and its handler are set up before any later scheduling or use, preventing uninitialized work usage at runtime.

intent_record.intent_summary: Cancel vbus_draw_work during DWC3 removal before dropping usb_psy to prevent teardown races and stale work accessing released power-supply resources.
intent_record.what: In dwc3_core_remove(), the single-line conditional around power_supply_put(dwc->usb_psy) was expanded into a block, and a new call to cancel_work_sync(&dwc->vbus_draw_work) was added before power_supply_put(dwc->usb_psy) inside the existing if (dwc->usb_psy) check.
intent_record.how: At runtime, when the DWC3 core is removed and a usb_psy power supply object exists, any pending or running vbus_draw_work is now synchronously cancelled before releasing the power supply reference. This prevents the work item from executing after or during release of usb_psy-related resources, avoiding potential use-after-free or teardown races.

intent_record.intent_summary: Document the vbus_draw_work and current_limit struct members by adding descriptive kernel-doc comments.
intent_record.what: Two documentation lines were added to the struct field comment block, introducing descriptions for @vbus_draw_work as work to set the VBUS drawing limit and @current_limit as the amount of current to draw from VBUS in milliamperes.
intent_record.how: This does not change runtime behavior; it improves source-level documentation by describing two existing struct members so developers can better understand their purpose.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add driver state for deferred VBUS draw processing and USB current limit tracking in struct dwc3.
intent_record.what: Two new fields were added to struct dwc3: a struct work_struct named vbus_draw_work and an unsigned int named current_limit.
intent_record.how: This extends the dwc3 device state so the driver can track a USB current limit value and schedule deferred work related to VBUS power draw handling at runtime.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove unused local variables from `dwc3_gadget_vbus_draw()` without changing its behavior.
intent_record.what: Two local variables, `union power_supply_propval val = {0};` and `int ret;`, were removed from `dwc3_gadget_vbus_draw()` while the existing logic and return paths shown in the hunk were left unchanged.
intent_record.how: This does not change the visible runtime behavior in the shown code path; it eliminates unused local declarations, reducing dead code and avoiding unused-variable compiler warnings.

intent_record.intent_summary: Defer DWC3 VBUS current-limit updates to scheduled work and make the gadget callback succeed after queuing the change.
intent_record.what: The function no longer converts mA to microamps and directly calls power_supply_set_property(); instead it stores mA in dwc->current_limit, schedules dwc->vbus_draw_work, removes use of the local ret result from the power supply update, and now always returns 0 after the usb_psy presence check.
intent_record.how: At runtime, VBUS current-limit changes are now deferred to an asynchronous work item rather than being applied immediately in this function. This avoids returning errors from power_supply_set_property() here and makes the gadget callback report success once the request is queued, while preserving the unsupported case when no usb_psy exists.

grouping_result.intent: Add driver state for deferred VBUS draw processing and USB current limit tracking in struct dwc3.
Defer DWC3 VBUS current-limit updates to scheduled work and make the gadget callback succeed after queuing the change.
Cancel vbus_draw_work during DWC3 removal before dropping usb_psy to prevent teardown races and stale work accessing released power-supply resources.
Document the vbus_draw_work and current_limit struct members by adding descriptive kernel-doc comments.
Remove unused local variables from `dwc3_gadget_vbus_draw()` without changing its behavior.

consistency_review.core_intent: Add DWC3 driver support for tracking USB current limit state and deferring VBUS/input current limit programming via work processing.
Defer DWC3 VBUS current-limit updates to scheduled work by initializing the required work item during USB power-supply setup and having the gadget callback queue the change successfully.

relevance_review.reason: The changes add deferred work and state tracking to handle VBUS/input current limit programming asynchronously instead of directly in the DWC3 path, which directly addresses the sleep-in-atomic issue caused by calling into the power supply framework from atomic context.

The changes directly address the root cause by moving VBUS current-limit updates out of the atomic gadget callback into deferred work, avoiding direct power_supply_set_property() calls from atomic context where sleeping is unsafe.

The change is about the same vbus_draw_work/power-supply interaction introduced to avoid calling power_supply_set_property() in atomic context. Canceling that work on removal prevents stale deferred power-supply updates from accessing usb_psy after teardown, so it directly relates to the fix path for the original bug.

The change only adds documentation comments for vbus_draw_work and current_limit struct members; it does not modify the atomic-context call to power_supply_set_property() or address the sleep-in-atomic bug.

The change only removes unused local variables in dwc3_gadget_vbus_draw() and explicitly does not alter behavior, so it does not address the atomic-context call to power_supply_set_property() or the sleep-in-atomic root cause.

candidates.rationale: This is the direct call into the power-supply subsystem from dwc3_gadget_vbus_draw(), and that path may sleep. Calling it from an atomic context is the root cause of the sleep-in-atomic bug.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement directly invokes the power-supply property update from dwc3_gadget_vbus_draw(), which can run in atomic context. Because power_supply_set_property() may sleep through the power-supply/PMIC stack, this call is the direct cause of the sleep-in-atomic vulnerability.

Per the stated root cause, directly invoking `power_supply_set_property()` from this callback is the problem because the power-supply/PMIC path may sleep while this callback can run in atomic context. There is no deferral to a workqueue or any other non-atomic handling; the code simply performs the call inline and returns `ret`. Therefore the vulnerable construct exists and the fix is not yet present.
